title: Grow a Garden
genre: Roblox idle/AFK farming simulator / social collect-and-trade (plant, harvest, sell, mutate crops, pets, trading, stealing)
release_date: 2025-03-26 (Roblox; Wikipedia gives 2025-03-26, Notebookcheck/Kotaku say 2025-03-25) [CONFIRMED – Roblox experience listing via Wikipedia/GamesBeat]
window_note: in window (launched March 2025, went viral May–Aug 2025; sequel Grow a Garden 2 launched May/June 2026)
developer: BMWLux (anonymous 16-year-old original creator) + Splitting Point Studios (Janzen 'Jandel' Madsen, New Zealand; lead dev Jhailatte / 'DJ Jai', Jandel's cousin) + Do Big Studios (Florida, minority partner). Rolimons/RoMonitor list the owning Roblox group as 'The Garden Game'.
team_size: Original build: 1 person (BMWLux) [CONFIRMED – Madsen via GameFile/Kotaku/PC Gamer]. Live-ops: ~12 devs – 'We staffed the game with almost all our [dev] staff (around 12 people)' [CONFIRMED – Madsen quoted in GameDiscoverCo newsletter, June 2025]. Splitting Point as a company later grew from ~10 to 50+ staff (just under half in NZ) [CONFIRMED – Madsen LinkedIn post via NZ media]; share working on Grow a Garden not disclosed. Do Big Studios headcount on the game: no data.
country: Original creator: unknown (anonymous teen). Splitting Point Studios: New Zealand (Nelson, remote-first). Do Big Studios: USA (Florida).
developer_background: BMWLux: anonymous 16-year-old hobbyist; built the first version 'in like three days' and released it March 2025 [CONFIRMED – Madsen via GameFile/PC Gamer]. Jandel/Splitting Point: founded 2017; Madsen (28, from Nelson NZ) earned $2 from his first Roblox game in 2017, ~$40k/yr by 2020 and 'six figures per month' by 2023 (Business Insider via NZ media); the studio has shipped 25–50+ Roblox games and runs an 'operator' model: scout small games early, buy a stake, add live-ops and weekly updates. Splitting Point partnered when the game had roughly 500–1,000 CCU / 10–20k DAU (April 2025).
publisher: Splitting Point Studios (co-owner/operator) with Do Big Studios (minority share, development and distribution partner); BMWLux retains ~50% ['like 50 percent of the game' – Madsen via GameFile/Kotaku; CONFIRMED as a dev statement, exact split not disclosed]. Dev/publisher revenue split unknown.
platforms_and_store_links: Roblox (PC, Mac, iOS, Android, Xbox, PlayStation, Meta Quest via Roblox client): https://www.roblox.com/games/126884695634066/Grow-a-Garden ; Rolimons: https://www.rolimons.com/game/126884695634066 ; RoMonitor: https://romonitorstats.com/experience/126884695634066/ ; Sequel Grow a Garden 2: https://www.rolimons.com/game/97598239454123
business_model: Free-to-play Roblox experience. Monetization via Robux developer products (seed packs / rare seeds, shop restocks, instant growth/skip timers, pet eggs, gear, gifting) and game passes, plus Roblox Premium engagement payouts. Also brand deals/merch: Roblox toy line and a film adaptation announced with Story Kitchen (2025-11-05) [CONFIRMED – Wikipedia/GamesBeat].
units_or_downloads: ~35.96 billion lifetime visits, ~11.4 million favourites [ESTIMATE – Rolimons snapshot, ~Sep/Oct 2026]; RoMonitor: ~35.9B visits, 11,436,820 favourites, #5 on all-time visits leaderboard [ESTIMATE – RoMonitor, ~Oct 2026]. Earlier: ~10B visits by ~June 2025 (PC Gamer); ~30B total plays (Madsen via GamesBeat, mid-2025). DAU: '~60 million peak, I think' [CONFIRMED-ish – Madsen via GamesBeat, hedged statement]; one of five Roblox experiences with >10M daily users in July 2025 [CONFIRMED – Roblox Q2 2025 earnings call].
peak_concurrent_players: 22,346,725 on 2025-08-23 [CONFIRMED – Roblox-tracking account RTC on X; Wikipedia gives 22.3M; Rolimons ~22.4M; a fan guide gives 22,375,597] – during the staged 'admin war' cross-event with Steal a Brainrot. Earlier milestones: >5M on 2025-05-17 (Notebookcheck); 8.9M late May 2025 (PC Gamer/GameDiscoverCo); >16M mid-June; 21,334,520 on 2025-06-21 (21.6M per Roblox), beating Fortnite's 15.3M record. Record later lost to Steal a Brainrot (Sept 2025). Baseline between events in June 2025 was 2–3M CCU (GameDiscoverCo). Recent: ~13k–99k CCU snapshots in Sep/Oct 2026 (Rolimons/RoWatcher) – heavy decline.
steam_reviews: n/a (Roblox). Roblox rating: 9,423,882 likes / 1,053,476 dislikes ≈ 89.9% positive [ESTIMATE – Rolimons/RoMonitor snapshot ~Oct 2026].
gross_revenue: Reported/tracker figures: ~$12M consumer spend in May 2025 alone [ESTIMATE – third-party (CreatorExchange analytics) reported by Calcalist and GameDaily]; '~$20M/month at peak' circulates on social media [unverified, no primary source]. Trackers: profitable.app lifetime model $286.8M with 30-day $381.2K (Sep 2026) – NOTE its model (visits × 2% × 150 Robux × 70% × $0.0038) is effectively creator-side DevEx value, not consumer spend; RoWatcher ~$1.75M/month (confidence 0.81, date unclear). Own estimate of lifetime consumer spend (Mar 2025–Sep 2026): ~$150M–$400M [ESTIMATE – $12M May 2025 anchor scaled by CCU: ~$15–35M/month Jun–Aug 2025, ~$5–15M/month Sep–Dec 2025, ~$1–5M/month 2026; cross-check: Roblox Q3 2025 bookings $1.92B, a ~4–6% share for the #1 spending experience ≈ $25–40M/month]. Roblox itself said it became the top experience by spending within a month of release [CONFIRMED – Roblox Q2 2025 earnings].
net_revenue: Net to all owners combined ≈ 25–30% of consumer spend → ~$40M–$120M lifetime (Mar 2025–Sep 2026); peak months ~$4–10M/month; ~$3–3.6M for May 2025 [ESTIMATE – spec Roblox method: ~70% creator share of Robux spent, DevEx ≈ $0.0038/Robux]. Split between BMWLux (~50%), Splitting Point and Do Big Studios not disclosed. Splitting Point: 'We don't disclose revenue publicly' [CONFIRMED – Madsen to NZ Herald].
production_cost: Original build: ~3 days solo by a teenager – effectively $0 cash (opportunity cost only) [CONFIRMED dev time via Madsen]. Live-ops since April 2025: ~12 devs × ~18 months × ~$6k/month ≈ $1.3M (range $0.9–2M incl. Do Big Studios contributions and event content) [ESTIMATE – spec method, NZ lean-indie rate]. Hosting/servers are paid by Roblox; no store fee. Acquisition price for Splitting Point's stake: no data (equity deal, not disclosed).
development_time: Original: ~3 days ('in like three days') [CONFIRMED – Madsen via GameFile/PC Gamer]. Viral ramp: Splitting Point joined at ~500–1,000 CCU (April 2025) → ~100k CCU within two weeks → 1M CCU in about a month [CONFIRMED – Madsen via GamesBeat]. Weekly updates every Saturday 7am PST since spring 2025 [CONFIRMED – GameDiscoverCo].
why_popular: Universal, low-stress fantasy ('everyone likes to farm, to watch something grow' – Madsen). Key hook: crops keep growing while you are offline – unusual on Roblox – so players log back in to harvest (strong D1/D7 retention). Non-competitive, cozy, kid-friendly loop: plant → wait → harvest → sell → buy better seeds. Variable-reward layers: random weather events (rain, snow, thunderstorm, Blood Moon, meteor showers) give crop mutations with value multipliers; rare seeds and pets; limited-time events. Social layer: visiting/stealing from other players' plots, trading, flexing rare mutations. Live 'admin abuse' events where Jandel joins servers and triggers rare weather (e.g. Meteoric x125 mutation) create FOMO and CCU spikes. Cross-promo 'admin war' with Steal a Brainrot on 2025-08-23 set the record. Note on fatigue: later criticism of repetitive weekly events and mutation clutter; the team announced a 'new era' and a dedicated events squad (PC Gamer).
marketing_channels: TikTok (player clips of rare mutations and admin events; Jandel has ~12M TikTok followers per Madsen), YouTube Roblox creators, Discord (update/event announcements), fixed weekly update schedule (Saturday 7am PST) that concentrates players into synchronized peaks, Roblox algorithmic discovery (Discover sorts, recommendations rewarding retention and session time; ~75% of its players also visited another experience the same day per Roblox), cross-promotional events with other top games (Steal a Brainrot 'admin war'). Operator model: early acquisition by an experienced live-ops studio. Press amplification in mainstream media (AP, Fortune, Kotaku) once records fell.
art_style: Bright, simple low-poly Roblox style; cartoony crops, plots and pets; mostly stock Roblox parts and simple meshes; UI-heavy shop/inventory screens.
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write virtually all Luau (plot ownership, timestamp-based offline growth via DataStoreService, seed shop with timed restocks, weather/mutation RNG, pets, trading/steal mechanics, MarketplaceService dev products and game passes, leaderboards); Roblox Assistant + Claude Code (via Rojo) are strong at Luau; low-poly crops/pets via Meshy/Tripo or the free Creator Store; UI icons via image gen; SFX/music via ElevenLabs/Suno (or Roblox's free audio library). Roblox handles hosting, matchmaking and replication, so multiplayer is cheap. The original was built solo in ~3 days. AI cannot: design a compelling economy and mutation/rarity tables, balance growth timers vs monetization, run weekly live-ops for months, plan admin events, prevent dupes/exploits in trading, build a TikTok/Discord community, or win Roblox's algorithm – this is what Splitting Point actually added. Copycats flood within days ('Grow a ...' clones), so speed + update cadence matter more than the code. Toolset: Roblox Studio + Luau + Rojo + Claude Code (Pro/Max), Roblox Assistant, Creator Store free models, Meshy/Tripo (3D), Midjourney/Scenario (thumbnails/icons), ElevenLabs SFX, Suno music, Roblox Ads/Sponsored Experiences for initial traffic.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 1–3 weeks, ~$50–$300 (Claude Pro/Max $20–$100/mo, optional 3D/image gen $20–$60, Roblox Studio free, no store fee; excludes the developer's own living costs)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 2–4 months to a live-ops-ready version (pets, trading, weather/mutations, events, anti-exploit), ~$1,500–$8,000 (AI tools $60–$250/mo, freelance thumbnail/icon art $200–$1,000, Roblox Ads/Sponsored Experiences test budget $500–$5,000, TikTok/YouTube creator promos optional). Ongoing: weekly updates are mandatory to hold algorithmic placement. Excludes own living costs.

data_conflicts: Peak CCU: 22,346,725 (RTC) vs 22.3M (Wikipedia/GamesBeat) vs ~22.4M (Rolimons) vs 22,375,597 (fan guide) – chose 22.35M on 2025-08-23. June record: 21,334,520 / 21.3M (RTC/Fortune) vs 21.6M (Roblox) – trackers differ in sampling. Release date: 2025-03-26 (Wikipedia/GamesBeat) vs 2025-03-25 (Notebookcheck). Stake date: April 2025 (Wikipedia) vs a blog's 'April 2026' (clearly a typo). Splitting Point entry point: ~500 CCU (GamesBeat) vs ~1,000 CCU (Wikipedia/GameDiscoverCo). Team: ~12 devs on the game (GameDiscoverCo, mid-2025) vs company totals of 19 devs / later 50+ staff. Revenue: estimates span $381K–$1.75M/month (2026 trackers) to $12M (May 2025) and unverified ~$20M/month peaks; profitable.app's $286.8M lifetime is a generic visits-based model and looks high versus the $12M/month anchor – I used my own range and labelled it ESTIMATE. Ownership after 2026: reports that Jandel stepped back from the 'owner' role (Discord) and that someone else (names 'Adrian'/'DevNamedDavid' circulate) runs the original game are unverified fan/blog claims. Grow a Garden 2 developer: Rolimons lists 'Strawberreh Squad'; some blogs say Splitting Point/Jandel is behind it, others say there is no evidence – unresolved.
notes: Grow a Garden 2 (sequel): released ~2026-05-21 per tracker listings (some coverage says late May/June 2026; Jandel publicly teased a sequel end of May 2026); developer group listed as 'Strawberreh Squad'; >400k CCU within 20 minutes of launch (GosuGamers); all-time peak 929,371 (Rolimons) / 971,967 on 2026-06-18 (HowManyArePlaying) / ~976k (RoWatcher) / 687,572 (GGAID); ~1.68B visits, 663,258 favourites, 87.87% rating (Rolimons, ~Oct 2026); steep decline since (down ~91% over 30 days by Sep 2026, ~2.7k CCU on 2026-09-27 per profitable.app). The sequel peaked at ~4% of the original's record – sequels do not reliably recapture a viral moment. Other: won 'Best New Experience' at the 2025 Roblox Innovation Awards; film adaptation announced with Story Kitchen (2025-11-05); Roblox toy line. Lessons for a solo creator: (1) the viral seed was a 3-day solo prototype – the value was in the hook (offline growth + mutations + social flex); (2) the scale came from an experienced operator adding weekly live-ops, events and algorithm optimisation – a solo dev should either commit to weekly updates or be open to partnering with a Roblox operator studio (Splitting Point, Do Big, etc.) that takes equity; (3) Roblox payouts mean only ~25–30% of player spend reaches creators; (4) DevEx requires age 13+, ID verification and a minimum earned-Robux balance; (5) clones appear within days, so first-mover speed and update cadence are the moat.
